previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain following a dialysis session and recent thrombectomy of her AV graft. Initial evaluation revealed a subsegmental pulmonary embolism on CT angiography, with no evidence of acute myocardial infarction despite a mildly elevated troponin and EKG changes. A pharmacologic stress test showed no ischemia, and her cardiac function was preserved with a normal ejection fraction. The chest pain was attributed to the pulmonary embolism and a separate component of musculoskeletal chest wall pain. Her dialysis access was evaluated with a fistulagram, which confirmed patency without thrombosis but identified a duplicated small-caliber brachial artery as the cause of low flow. She was anticoagulated with a heparin bridge to warfarin, which was continued at discharge. The patient remained stable, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged to extended care with follow-up planned for anticoagulation management, transplant surgery, and orthopedics.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Left-sided chest pain.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: AP upright and lateral chest radiographs were obtained.  The lungs
are low in volume but clear.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. 
The heart is stably enlarged which post CABG changes noted.

IMPRESSION: No acute intrathoracic process.

HISTORY:  Chest pain and subtherapeutic INR, assess for pulmonary embolus.

TECHNIQUE:  CT images were obtained through the chest in arterial phase after
the uneventful intravenous administration of 100 cc of the contrast medium. 
Multiplanar reformations were prepared.  

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: The thyroid gland is normal with symmetric enhancement.  The aorta
and major branches are patent and normal in caliber with mild atherosclerotic
calcification as well as mild aortic valvular calcification.  Post CABG
changes are noted with moderate to severe coronary vascular calcification. 
Left ventricular hypertrophy is noted along with mild cardiomegaly.  There is
no pleural or pericardial effusion.  Small hiatal hernia is noted.  The
pulmonary arterial tree is well opacified without evidence of filling defect
to suggest pulmonary embolus.  The previously seen subsegmental right lower
lobe pulmonary embolus appears to have resolved.  The trachea and central
airways are patent to the segmental level.  The lungs are well expanded
without focal consolidation.  Subsegmental atelectasis is seen dependently. 
Although the study is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, the imaged
upper abdomen is unremarkable.  Postsurgical changes are seen along the
anterior chest wall.  There is no mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymph node
enlargement.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no suspicious lytic or blastic bony focus to
suggest osseous malignancy with mild multilevel spinal degenerative changes.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No pulmonary embolism or acute aortic pathology. Previously seen
subsegmental right lower lobe pulmonary embolus has resolved.

2.  Post CABG with severe coronary vascular calcifications
